skill.description: Build LI.FI integrations for cross-chain swaps, bridges, DeFi deposits, yield discovery, transaction tracking, and intent-based transfers through documented REST APIs.

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown and template-literal syntax. LI.FI HTTP calls are real, intended network capabilities that expose transaction metadata to LI.FI. Two high-risk workflow gaps remain: no explicit final transaction-confirmation gate and insufficient controls for arbitrary contract calls.

remediation.issue: Asset-moving transactions can be approved or signed without a documented final confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation after showing chain, token, exact amount, recipient, spender, fee, minimum received, and decoded calldata.

remediation.issue: Manual contract-call routes lack mandatory validation controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require simulation, calldata decoding, trusted contract allowlists, and a separate user confirmation before signing.

remediation.issue: Earn API examples can encourage client-side API key handling.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Earn API keys server-side, document required authentication on every Earn example, and redact keys from logs.

content.value_statement: Cross-chain swaps and DeFi flows require route, token, chain, and transaction handling. This skill helps you use LI.FI APIs to build and operate these flows with documented endpoints and checks.
actual_capabilities: Request LI.FI quotes and routes for same-chain swaps and cross-chain transfers.
Query supported chains, tokens, bridges, exchanges, gas prices, and route tools.
Build Composer flows for supported swap, bridge, deposit, stake, lend, and withdrawal operations.
Discover Earn vaults, APY, TVL, protocols, and tokenized positions.
Track transaction status, partial completions, refunds, and recovery paths.
Integrate solver-based intent quotes, order submission, and order status checks.
limitations: Does not custody assets or sign transactions for users.
API quotes, routes, token support, and protocol availability can change.
Cross-chain transfers can fail, refund, or complete partially.
Earn API access requires an API key and server-side secret handling.

use_cases.title: Add bridge routing to an application
use_cases.description: Request routes, display trade details, and hand approved transaction data to a wallet flow.

use_cases.title: Monitor transfer recovery
use_cases.description: Check transfer status and present next steps for pending, partial, refunded, or failed transfers.

use_cases.title: Discover deposit opportunities
use_cases.description: Find supported vaults and prepare Composer routes for reviewed DeFi deposits.

prompt_templates.title: Find a swap quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Get a LI.FI quote for swapping a specified token amount on one chain. Show fees, minimum received, and route details. Do not sign or send a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Compare bridge routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare LI.FI routes for transferring a specified token between two chains. Rank by estimated time and cost. Flag slippage and approval requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Build safe transfer monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LI.FI transfer-status workflow with bounded backoff, persistent transaction hashes, and clear handling for partial, refunded, and failed results.

prompt_templates.title: Review Composer deposit transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a LI.FI Composer deposit quote. Decode and summarize transaction effects, recipient, spender, fees, slippage, and minimum received. Require confirmation before signing.

output_examples.input: Compare routes for a stablecoin bridge between two named chains.
output: Route comparison with estimated time and cost.
Recommendation marked as informational until user confirmation.

output_examples.input: Check a submitted transfer by transaction hash.
output: Recovery guidance for pending, partial, refunded, or failed outcomes.
Reminder to retain transaction hash and confirm final balances.

output_examples.input: Find a supported yield vault for a token.
output: Matching vaults with protocol, chain, APY, and TVL.
Instruction to review deposit transaction before signing.

best_practices: Re-quote immediately before signing because routes and prices can change.
Show users transaction fields and require explicit confirmation before approval or signing.
Store API keys server-side and never place them in browser code or logs.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-sign, auto-approve, or auto-submit asset-moving transactions.
Do not trust arbitrary calldata without decoding, simulation, allowlisting, and user review.
Do not treat a timeout as a failed transfer; check status and final balances.

faq.question: Does this skill move assets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents LI.FI integration workflows. Users must review and approve wallet actions.

faq.question: Is a LI.FI API key required?
faq.answer: Core API access can work without a key. Earn requests require an API key and should run server-side.

faq.question: Can it support same-chain swaps?
faq.answer: Yes. LI.FI quotes can describe same-chain swaps and cross-chain transfers.

faq.question: What should happen before signing?
faq.answer: Review chain, token, amount, recipient, spender, fee, minimum received, and decoded calldata. Then obtain explicit confirmation.

faq.question: What happens if a bridge partially completes?
faq.answer: Check status and balances. A partial result can deliver a different token or require a same-chain recovery swap.

faq.question: Can it discover DeFi yields?
faq.answer: Yes. Earn endpoints provide supported vault, protocol, APY, TVL, and position data.
